power.title: Power Analysis Check
report:
::: {.callout-tip title="Learn More" collapse="true"}

Power analyses need to contain the following information to be interpretable: the type of power analysis, the statistical test, the software used, sample size, critical alpha criterion, power level, effect size, and an effect size metric. In addition, it is recommended to make sure the power analysis is reproducible (by sharing the code, or a screenshot, of the power analysis), and to provide good arguments for why the study was designed to detect an effect of this size.

For an a-priori power analysis, where the sample size is determined, reporting all information would look like:

> An a priori power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that for a Cohen's d = 0.5, an alpha level of 0.05, and a desired power level of 80% required at least 64 participants in each group.

For a sensitivity power analysis, this sentence would look like:

> A sensitivity power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that with 64 participants in each group, and an alpha level of 0.05, a desired power level of 80% was reached for an effect size of d = 0.5.

info.title: The AI Paradox: How Optimization May Undermine Meaningful Work in Helping Professions

text.text: Helping professions are adopting artificial intelligence (AI) to automate documentation, monitoring, and coordination on the premise that offloading routine tasks frees workers for meaningful care.
That premise assumes managers know which tasks are routine and which meaningful.
We argue instead for a task-contingent AI paradox: meaning in helping work concentrates in identity-central tasks that are increasingly automatable.

Study 1, a two-wave critical-incident panel of 307 helping-profession workers (144 longitudinal cases one year later), tested six pre-specified predictions that Time 1 human-coded meaning dimensions forecast Time 2 felt meaningfulness, exhaustion, or turnover intentions; estimates were near zero, and equivalence at the |β| = .30 sensitivity band held for three of five.

One exploratory association survived multiplicity screening: narratives grounding meaning in competence were associated with higher later turnover intentions and exhaustion (β = .29 and .30, adjusting for six survey measures).
Automated coding did not reach the human-agreement standard; humans coded all predictors.
Study 2 coded 7,695 nursing-forum posts captured 2016-2026 for meaning events.

Nurses named AI in seven events; about one post in twenty per period instead named an optimization or implementation object (ratios, metrics, dashboards, documentation load), and the facet at issue was control over means.
Study 3 found that share unchanged across the decade; the one strain marker that rose, lacking control, is confounded with a site template change.
No study measured individual AI exposure.
Against the automation frontier, the results locate the risk of optimization in the tasks workers name as meaningful, not in AI as such.
Organizations in helping professions increasingly treat artificial intelligence (AI) as a way to shift routine work away from clinicians so they can focus on high-value care.

Ambient AI documentation tools are associated with lower documentation burden, note-writing time, and after-hours charting, and their adoption with lower burnout and more undivided attention to patients (Albrecht et al., 2025; Lukac et al., 2025; Olson et al., 2025; Shah et al., 2025; Tierney et al., 2024; You et al., 2025).
text.formatted: Ambient AI documentation tools are associated with lower documentation burden, note-writing time, and after-hours charting, and their adoption with lower burnout and more undivided attention to patients <ref type="bibr" target="#b0">(Albrecht et al., 2025;</ref> <ref type="bibr" target="#b43">Lukac et al., 2025;</ref> <ref type="bibr" target="#b51">Olson et al., 2025;</ref> <ref type="bibr" target="#b67">Shah et al., 2025;</ref> <ref type="bibr" target="#b75">Tierney et al., 2024;</ref> <ref type="bibr" target="#b88">You et al., 2025)</ref>.

text.text: Health systems adopt ambient documentation, predictive monitoring, and automated care coordination under this banner.
They frame the result as restoring the human side of care (Olson et al., 2025; Tierney et al., 2024).
text.formatted: They frame the result as restoring the human side of care <ref type="bibr" target="#b51">(Olson et al., 2025;</ref> <ref type="bibr" target="#b75">Tierney et al., 2024)</ref>.

text.text: The premise is intuitive.
It rests on an untested assumption: that managers already know which tasks are routine, which are meaningful, and that the two can be cleanly separated.
Field evidence shows that the routine-meaningful boundary can cut through tasks labeled as efficient targets for automation.
When UC Davis Health piloted a wearable biosensor system to automate continuous patient monitoring in an oncology unit, it discontinued the device after roughly a year (Schellmann, 2026).
text.formatted: When UC Davis Health piloted a wearable biosensor system to automate continuous patient monitoring in an oncology unit, it discontinued the device after roughly a year <ref type="bibr" target="#b66">(Schellmann, 2026)</ref>.

text.text: Nurses reported detecting deterioration faster than the algorithm in the sickest patients, using cues the sensors could not capture, and the hospital concluded that the alerts offered no clear advantage over existing monitoring (Schellmann, 2026).
text.formatted: Nurses reported detecting deterioration faster than the algorithm in the sickest patients, using cues the sensors could not capture, and the hospital concluded that the alerts offered no clear advantage over existing monitoring <ref type="bibr" target="#b66">(Schellmann, 2026)</ref>.

text.text: Frontline accounts of clinical AI report a similar pattern elsewhere: when algorithmic alerts misfire or cannot explain themselves, nurses carry residual risk and close the judgment gap (Schellmann, 2026).
text.formatted: Frontline accounts of clinical AI report a similar pattern elsewhere: when algorithmic alerts misfire or cannot explain themselves, nurses carry residual risk and close the judgment gap <ref type="bibr" target="#b66">(Schellmann, 2026)</ref>.

text.text: What optimization had classified as automatable monitoring proved to be professional judgment central to nursing identity.
The episode is what Siggelkow (2007) called a "talking pig": a single instance establishing that a routine-meaningful boundary can run through a task automated in the name of efficiency.
text.formatted: The episode is what <ref type="bibr" target="#b68">Siggelkow (2007)</ref> called a "talking pig": a single instance establishing that a routine-meaningful boundary can run through a task automated in the name of efficiency.

text.text: If that boundary is misdrawn, optimization saves time and removes occasions for meaning.
In helping professions, meaning is part of the psychological infrastructure that sustains the workforce rather than a mere perquisite of the job (Bunderson & Thompson, 2009).
text.formatted: In helping professions, meaning is part of the psychological infrastructure that sustains the workforce rather than a mere perquisite of the job <ref type="bibr" target="#b9">(Bunderson & Thompson, 2009)</ref>.

text.text: Automation may have an iatrogenic effect in helping professions if it is implemented without knowing which tasks carry meaning.
Those occupations already face chronic vacancies and attrition.
The pipeline depends on intrinsic rewards to offset job costs.
Federal projections anticipate national shortages of registered nurses through at least 2038.
The same horizon includes shortfalls of roughly 100,000 mental health counselors, 77,000 addiction counselors, and 44,000 psychiatrists (National Center for Health Workforce Analysis, 2025a, 2025b).
Exposure to robots and AI is associated with job insecurity and maladaptive workplace behavior (Yam et al., 2023).
text.formatted: Exposure to robots and AI is associated with job insecurity and maladaptive workplace behavior <ref type="bibr" target="#b87">(Yam et al., 2023)</ref>.

text.text: Insecurity about the automation of occupational content, as distinct from job loss, is associated with burnout and health complaints (Roll et al., 2025).
text.formatted: Insecurity about the automation of occupational content, as distinct from job loss, is associated with burnout and health complaints <ref type="bibr" target="#b62">(Roll et al., 2025)</ref>.

text.text: Insecurity from human-AI collaboration spills into work-life outcomes (Wu et al., 2024).
text.formatted: Insecurity from human-AI collaboration spills into work-life outcomes <ref type="bibr" target="#b86">(Wu et al., 2024)</ref>.

text.text: Comparing oneself with AI coworkers is one reported burnout path (Ma & Li, 2026).
text.formatted: Comparing oneself with AI coworkers is one reported burnout path <ref type="bibr" target="#b44">(Ma & Li, 2026)</ref>.

text.text: Adoption framed as substitution rather than augmentation is associated with lower willingness to stay among caregivers (Jiang et al., 2026).
text.formatted: Adoption framed as substitution rather than augmentation is associated with lower willingness to stay among caregivers <ref type="bibr" target="#b34">(Jiang et al., 2026)</ref>.

text.text: If the tasks automated to reduce burnout are the tasks through which workers experience meaning, then efficiency optimization can become self-defeating.
We name that possibility a task-contingent AI paradox.
The proposed mechanism is a diseconomy of scale in meaning: efficiency gains from automating meaning-critical tasks may be offset by losses in the psychological resources that sustain the workforce.
The question this article addresses is not whether AI can make helping work faster but which tasks are meaning-critical and what follows when those tasks are automated.
Dominant scholarly and practitioner accounts rarely pose that question; they answer it by assumption.
Reviews of AI across helping professions converge on a division of labor.
AI absorbs documentation, monitoring, triage, decision support, and administrative coordination.

Professionals are then freed for direct care, complex judgment, and compassionate interaction (Balan & Gumpel, 2025; Garkisch & Goldkind, 2024; Guo et al., 2024; Han et al., 2026; Hobensack et al., 2024).
text.formatted: Professionals are then freed for direct care, complex judgment, and compassionate interaction <ref type="bibr" target="#b2">(Balan & Gumpel, 2025;</ref> <ref type="bibr" target="#b23">Garkisch & Goldkind, 2024;</ref> <ref type="bibr" target="#b28">Guo et al., 2024;</ref> <ref type="bibr" target="#b30">Han et al., 2026;</ref> <ref type="bibr" target="#b32">Hobensack et al., 2024)</ref>.

text.text: Empirical evidence for this narrative concentrates on the clerical side.
Automating documentation is associated with lower burden and burnout (Albrecht et al., 2025; Olson et al., 2025; Shah et al., 2025; You et al., 2025).
text.formatted: Automating documentation is associated with lower burden and burnout <ref type="bibr" target="#b0">(Albrecht et al., 2025;</ref> <ref type="bibr" target="#b51">Olson et al., 2025;</ref> <ref type="bibr" target="#b67">Shah et al., 2025;</ref> <ref type="bibr" target="#b88">You et al., 2025)</ref>.

text.text: Reviews of AI workplace outcomes give little attention to meaning and purpose (Bankins et al., 2024; Pereira et al., 2023).
text.formatted: Reviews of AI workplace outcomes give little attention to meaning and purpose <ref type="bibr" target="#b5">(Bankins et al., 2024;</ref> <ref type="bibr" target="#b57">Pereira et al., 2023)</ref>.

text.text: Conceptual treatments often position automation as a net enabler of meaning when deployment is well governed (Bankins & Formosa, 2023; Smids et al., 2020).
text.formatted: Conceptual treatments often position automation as a net enabler of meaning when deployment is well governed <ref type="bibr" target="#b4">(Bankins & Formosa, 2023;</ref> <ref type="bibr" target="#b70">Smids et al., 2020)</ref>.

text.text: The few studies that measure experienced meaningfulness under AI-related job change are recent, largely cross-sectional, and outside flagship industrial-organizational journals (Callari & Puppione, 2025; Gemmano et al., 2026; Liu et al., 2026).
text.formatted: The few studies that measure experienced meaningfulness under AI-related job change are recent, largely cross-sectional, and outside flagship industrial-organizational journals <ref type="bibr" target="#b10">(Callari & Puppione, 2025;</ref> <ref type="bibr" target="#b24">Gemmano et al., 2026;</ref> <ref type="bibr" target="#b40">Liu et al., 2026)</ref>.

text.text: This literature rests on a shared assumption: that the routine-meaningful partition of tasks is known, stable, and aligned with what can be automated.
That assumption is asserted more often than examined.
Two lines of evidence convert the efficiency story into a theoretical tension.
Meaning at work is task-contingent and identity-central.
It concentrates in particular activities rather than spreading evenly across a job, a reading that follows from the pathway structure Rosso et al. (2010) describe.
text.formatted: It concentrates in particular activities rather than spreading evenly across a job, a reading that follows from the pathway structure <ref type="bibr" target="#b63">Rosso et al. (2010)</ref> describe.

text.text: Automation effects show the same granularity.
Generative AI produces large gains on tasks inside its capability frontier and degrades performance on adjacent tasks just outside it (Dell'Acqua et al., 2026).
text.formatted: Generative AI produces large gains on tasks inside its capability frontier and degrades performance on adjacent tasks just outside it <ref type="bibr" target="#b15">(Dell'Acqua et al., 2026)</ref>.

text.text: Several tasks now targeted for automation plausibly carry meaning.
Automating monitoring, documentation, and analysis can shrink the task identity and problem-solving that underpin clinicians' intrinsic motivation (Bienefeld et al., 2025).
text.formatted: Automating monitoring, documentation, and analysis can shrink the task identity and problem-solving that underpin clinicians' intrinsic motivation <ref type="bibr" target="#b7">(Bienefeld et al., 2025)</ref>.

text.text: Diagnostic AI intersects the autonomous judgment that professionals defend as central to responsibility (Faulconbridge et al., 2025; Lebovitz et al., 2022).
text.formatted: Diagnostic AI intersects the autonomous judgment that professionals defend as central to responsibility <ref type="bibr" target="#b19">(Faulconbridge et al., 2025;</ref> <ref type="bibr" target="#b38">Lebovitz et al., 2022)</ref>.

text.text: Expecting one's work to be robotized is associated with lower meaningfulness and more burnout symptoms (Turja et al., 2022).
text.formatted: Expecting one's work to be robotized is associated with lower meaningfulness and more burnout symptoms <ref type="bibr" target="#b78">(Turja et al., 2022)</ref>.

text.text: Philosophers of technology describe related "achievement gaps" when machines absorb the accomplishments through which workers earn meaning (Danaher & Nyholm, 2021; Parmer, 2024).
text.formatted: Philosophers of technology describe related "achievement gaps" when machines absorb the accomplishments through which workers earn meaning <ref type="bibr" target="#b14">(Danaher & Nyholm, 2021;</ref> <ref type="bibr" target="#b56">Parmer, 2024)</ref>.

text.text: The relationship between meaning and well-being is not monotonic.
Deeply meaningful, calling-infused work can bind workers to self-sacrifice and exhaustion even as it confers purpose (Bunderson & Thompson, 2009; Cardador & Caza, 2012; Schabram & Maitlis, 2017).

text.text: The routine-meaningful dichotomy therefore fails on two counts: it mislocates where meaning resides, and it assumes that more meaning is uniformly better.
What replaces it is a contingency: the effect of automating a task depends on the task's meaning content and on how densely meaning is already concentrated in the work.

We make that contingency analytically tractable by anchoring in the most influential integrative account of why work becomes meaningful. Rosso et al. text.text: The architecture matters for the paradox.
Helping work is disproportionately other-oriented and draws meaning from Contribution and Unification pathways, impact on and connection to patients and community.
Those relational tasks are the ones the optimization narrative treats as most valuable.

text.text: The second is the direction of the meaning-conferring action, toward the self or toward others.

Crossing these yields four pathways: Individuation (self-agency; for example, competence, autonomy, and self-esteem realized through work), Contribution (other-agency; for example, significance, impact, and transcendence of self-interest in service of others), Self-Connection (self-communion; for example, authenticity and identity coherence), and Unification (other-communion; for example, shared values and belonging).

In the present project these pathways are operationalized through 13 binary facets, aggregated to the four pathways and then to the 2 × 2 superordinate dimensions using an inclusive (logical-OR) rule.

Automating a meaning-critical task removes an occasion for meaning even as it frees the same time.
The effect of an efficiency intervention is therefore task-contingent, beneficial or harmful depending on the meaning content of the task it removes.

text.text: Aggregated across a workforce, systematically automating meaning-critical tasks yields what we term a diseconomy of scale in meaning.

text.text: Meaning anchored in others should therefore most strongly buffer the burnout component that shares its relational content.
Block 2 specifies confirmatory tests on the contrast-coded Agency-Communion and Self-Others dimensions and their interaction.
These tests distinguish Rosso et al.'s (2010) additive account from an interactive one.

text.text: The Self-Others contrast predicts T2 workforce-sustaining outcomes such that other-oriented T1 meaning is more strongly and positively associated with T2 wellbeing and engagement than self-oriented meaning.
Agency and Communion interact rather than combine purely additively in predicting T2 outcomes; the effect of one dimension depends on the level of the other (a nonadditive 2 × 2 interaction).

The Self-Others contrast differentially predicts burnout components: other-oriented T1 meaning is more strongly (inversely) associated with T2 depersonalization than with T2 emotional exhaustion; this difference warrants separate treatment of these subscales in this block.
Within the other-oriented dimension, the two pathways rest on theoretically distinct mechanisms.
Contribution operates through perceived impact and significance, the mechanism by which contact with beneficiaries fuels prosocial motivation and persistence (Grant, 2008a (Grant, , 2008b)).

text.text: Unification operates through shared values and belonging, the relational resources most directly threatened when algorithmic mediation weakens identity and connection at work (van Zoonen et al., 2024).

text.text: Outcome assignments follow these mechanisms.
Contribution's impact mechanism feeds motivational and affective outcomes.
Unification's belonging mechanism is an embedding force: shared values and connection bind workers to the setting that supplies them.
Unification, uniquely among the pathways, therefore carries the turnover and mobility prediction.
Block 3 tests whether these pathways carry the workforce-sustaining effects that the paradox would place at risk.

Block 4 tests the conjecture that "too many active pathways to meaning are exhausting and lead to burnout" (Rosso et al., 2010, p. 116), using the theorizing-and-testing guidelines for U-shaped relationships set out by Haans et al. (2016).

Six prompt configurations were developed exclusively on the training partition and fixed by SHA-256 hash before evaluation: a decision-first instruction and a revised decision-first instruction, a per-facet version that issued thirteen separate calls per narrative, a reason-first variant, a decision-plus-evidence variant, and an alternate-codebook variant.

Each prompt was evaluated once on the 55-case development partition under a selection rule fixed in advance: three replicates per prompt on the pre-specified primary model (claude-sonnet-5, run 2026-09-22), selection statistics computed on counts pooled across replicates, and case-level cluster bootstrap (B = 10,000, fixed seed) for all intervals.

Acceptance was calibrated to what human coders achieve.

The allnurses author pane displays the credential line members choose to publish (e.g., "BSN, RN," "MSN, APRN, NP," "LPN," "Nursing Student").

The pre-specified tests placed the year-ahead associations between narrated meaning dimensions and felt meaningfulness, exhaustion, and turnover intentions near zero; for next-year meaningfulness the Bayes factor (BF01 = 481.5) favors the null decisively.
The same codes were associated with self-reported meaningfulness in the same wave, which supports the concurrent validity of the coding scheme.
One prospective association survived screening: when Time 1 stories grounded meaning in competence or mastery, Time 2 turnover intentions and emotional exhaustion were higher.
That last result is exploratory and rests on 17 present-coded cases.
It was also the only coded feature that out-predicted the Time 1 survey battery for strain.
Two interpretations are consistent with the result.
Meaning that must be earned through demonstrated skill can become a contingent investment.
Meaning staked on mastery can also convert to restlessness when the job stops supplying growth.
Those readings treat the code as an anchor in the story.
Whether the underlying need was met is a different question; Martela and Riekki (2018) locate meaningfulness in competence need satisfaction, not in narrative mention of mastery alone.
Codes assigned from the abstract meaning answer but absent from the story were orthogonal to the story codes.

Studies 2 and 3 asked how a decade of nurses' own talk about their work relates to the account of the AI paradox developed in Study 1.
The first result is an informative absence.

Nurses rarely referred to artificial intelligence: seven events in 7,695 posts named an AI system, none in the 2023-2026 window, and AI vocabulary appeared in fewer than one post in a hundred in any year, including the years after generative tools entered wide public use.
A study that operationalized AI exposure as mention of AI would have detected nothing and would have misattributed the reason.

What nurses discussed, in a steady one post in twenty across ten years, were the instruments that measure and reorganize their tasks: ratios, productivity targets, dashboards, documentation load, and the arrival of new systems.
We interpret this as the phenomenon the AI-paradox literature describes, in the terms practitioners use for it.
The paradox as formulated here is not about a technology but about a mode of organizing work in which decisions about how a task is done migrate from the person doing it to a system that scores it.
Nurses have described that mode since before the current wave of tools, and their vocabulary for it is managerial and task-focused, not technological.

The implication for measurement is direct: exposure to algorithmic management in occupational text must be sought through the artefacts and practices themselves, not through the word "AI," which is a researcher's category rather than a worker's.
We do not claim from these data that AI is eroding meaning, or that any Rosso facet declined after 2023; the data show neither.
The second result concerns which facet carries the strain.
Across periods the cell that grew was frustrated Control/Autonomy, the flag that rose was lack of control, and half of all object events landed on Control/Autonomy.
Competence remained the most enacted facet in every period, and the communion-family facets were enacted far more often than frustrated.
In Rosso et al.'s (2010) terms, where an optimization object is named, the facet at issue is discretion over means, not skill.

text.text: Study 1's pre-specified agency paths were estimated near zero, so the prospective evidence available here is the one exploratory association that survived screening, and it runs from competence toward strain, not protection.
What Studies 2 and 3 add is descriptive.
Communion deserves a separate comment because it is both pervasive and hard to code, and those facts are related.
Communion vocabulary saturates the posts that carry any meaning event, but it rarely appears as a discrete episode with a polarity.

A sentence in which a nurse cannot give patients the care they deserve has care as its object and the blocked action as its marked feature; both human coders in Study 1 and the model here register it as frustrated Control, while the communion it presupposes goes uncoded.
We suggest this is why inter-coder agreement on Communion sits near .5 for humans and models alike (Study 1) and why the facet is dispersed across five low-frequency facets here.
That reading yields a hypothesis rather than a finding: the complaint arrives framed as autonomy loss because the injury is to communion, and autonomy over one's time is the means to it.
Testing it requires a measurement approach that treats communion as a property of the post rather than of the event.
Because Studies 2 and 3 are same-post co-occurrence designs in a self-selected venue, their implications concern measurement rather than intervention.
The relevant exposure in nursing is not the presence of an AI tool but the manner in which any system arrives: as a metric, a new documentation duty, or a management mandate.
Screening a deployment for what it does to the task (taken, added, reconfigured) and to discretion over means is consistent with the pattern here in a way that screening for "AI" is not.

The sense of lacking control is the only strain marker that moved over the decade; its co-occurrence with optimization talk in the same post is partly a property of the codebook and is not evidence of temporal order, so whether discretion over means is an earlier signal than burnout inventories is a question for a lagged, within-account design that has not been run.

Competence and relational connection are the meaning resources these data show still being enacted; deployments that displace skill or compress patient contact would act on the parts of the job that remain intact.
Several boundary conditions delimit the paradox.
Meaning is heterogeneous.
A task that is meaning-critical for one worker may be routine for another (Tang et al., 2022).

text.text: The paradox is a claim about distributions of meaning across a workforce, not a universal task ranking.
Economic context also matters.
In precarious conditions the most consequential feature of work may simply be having a job.
The diseconomy of scale we describe becomes decision-relevant when efficiency and retention are both at stake.
Finally, the claim is about meaning-critical tasks.
Where automation removes genuinely low-meaning work, the efficiency case is intact (Albrecht et al., 2025; Olson et al., 2025).

text.text: Study 1 establishes a meaning-criticality map, not a measured AI effect.
Its strengths are a year-lagged design, confirmatory tests at the more reliable dimensional level, and an attempt to test previously untested conjectures.
Its limitations are equally clear.
The Time 1 data predate the automation wave, so the paradox is read by juxtaposition.
The sample is an online panel and is majority, but not exclusively, health care.
Studies 2 and 3 widen the text base.
They do not resolve individual-level exposure.
We prefer that claim to a causal one the design cannot support.
Studies 2 and 3 carry their own limits.

The instrument is a single model applied once, without human coding of forum text and without second-model, perturbation, or negative-control checks, so the false-present rate on forum prose is unknown.

The frustration series is confounded with a page-template change that shortened posts and reduced codable events in 2019-2021; we report rising control loss with that caveat and do not claim rising frustration.
Period is capture period, not posting period.
The exposure-strain contrast compares complaint posts with all other posts and is partly circular by codebook design; most quit-flagged posts name no object.
The careerpoint badge is a capture-time credential with template-dependent coverage; aides and students are sparse in the venue after 2019.
The dictionaries are occupational vocabularies, not facet measures, and we draw no year-trend conclusion from them.

A within-account design over the 1,494 accounts with two or more posts, using posted rather than captured dates, is the analysis that would move "indicator" from a suggestion to a claim; it has not been run.
The engineered prompts fell short of an acceptance standard tied to human-human agreement, a result about this codebook and prompt set rather than a ceiling on machine coding.
Human agreement on communion and self-directed facets was itself low.
Prompts selected to match those labels can transmit that disagreement into the scores.

An independent panel that applies the same scheme without being fitted to a particular human pair, then evaluated against later well-being and retention rather than against human PSA, may give more accurate estimates than either the disqualified prompts or the human composite.
More accurate estimates may be more predictive.
That test is the next measurement study, not a result of this article.
A further limit is that the coding scheme records presence, not salience.
Human coders made binary judgments.
No graded measure of how central an anchor was to the story exists in these data.
The one machine attempt at such a measure did not meet the pre-set reliability bar.
Dichotomization at low base rates attenuates associations.
Under a normal liability model, the observed point-biserial correlations of .28 between competence codes and Time 2 strain imply latent continuous associations of .44 to .46 (Figure S8).

text.text: Those biserial estimates assume latent normality and are illustrative.
They suggest that the binary results are more likely to understate than overstate the underlying continuous associations.
The pre-specified tests, the concurrent convergence, and the competence-strain association constitute the findings.
The remaining screened tests bound how far those three can be interpreted.
In these data, no global meaning score forecast turnover intentions; the one prospective association involved the kind of meaning narrated, specifically competence, and next-year strain.
The optimization case for automating helping work still assumes a known split between routine and meaningful tasks.
The pre-specified dimensional map did not forecast next-year outcomes; its estimates were bounded near zero.
A decade of nurses' own talk named the instruments of optimization, not AI, and what rose in it, with the template-change caveat attached, was a sense of lacking control over means.
The competence result is the one that carried prospective signal, and it is the result a designed study should attempt to falsify.
